prompts.idle:
Use case: identity-preserve
Asset type: pixel-art game animation sprite sheet, chicken_idle.png.
Image 1 is the exact chicken character to animate (CHICKEN4.0.png, a 120x120 transparent pixel image). Image 2 is sheep idle motion reference; image 3 is sheep eating motion reference; image 4 is sheep run reference. Preserve the chicken in image 1, not the sheep.
Produce a single transparent horizontal strip with EXACTLY SIX evenly spaced square cells, one chicken per cell, all facing LEFT as in the original. Requested native atlas size 768x128, six 128x128 cells. Keep the chicken native sprite about 63x66 pixels with its original cream feathers, pale sage/blue lower-body shading, dark hand-drawn pixel outline, pale rounded wing with dark outline, tiny yellow beak, small red comb, small dark feet and tail pointing right. Consistent character identity and scale across all six frames, feet anchor centered at x=64 y=103 within each cell, with transparent padding. Hard crisp raster pixel art without anti-aliasing, no smooth painting, no redesign.
Animate only a restrained idle loop inspired by sheep's breathing: frame 1 neutral original pose; 2 slight chest inhale; 3 chest and wing lift one pixel; 4 relaxed blink at top of inhale; 5 eyes open and exhale; 6 settle almost to frame 1. Standing feet fixed on ground; tiny comb/tail secondary motion. The changes must be visible but subtle; no translated whole-sprite duplicates. Frame 6 loops cleanly to frame 1.
One row only, no grid lines, text, labels, numbers, decorative elements, grass, scene, shadow, floor or background. Actual alpha transparency, not checkerboard. Final deliverable is the atlas, no explanatory composition.
prompts.eating:
Use case: identity-preserve. Pixel-art animation sprite atlas for the exact chicken in reference image 1 CHICKEN4.0.png. Keep identical cream feather colors, muted sage/blue shading, tiny red comb, small yellow beak, dark pixel outlines, rounded outlined wing, dark thin legs, small upturned tail on right. Face LEFT in every frame. Crisp original pixel style, no smooth painting, no redesign. Image 2 is the matching newly created idle chicken sheet: preserve this same character. Image 3 is the sheep motion reference; use only its motion principles. Transparent alpha background. Consistent scale and ground anchor in every equal-sized cell. No text, cell borders, labels, grass, props, floor, shadows, or scenery.
Create chicken_eating.png with EXACTLY TWELVE animation frames in a regular grid of SIX COLUMNS and TWO ROWS of SQUARE CELLS. Read left to right through top row, then left to right through bottom row. Each frame has exactly one whole chicken, including feet, with generous transparent margins. Unlike a sheep, a chicken pecks by flexing its neck/head downward while the body tilts gently and feet remain planted. Frame 1 neutral upright. 2 anticipate with neck forward. 3 neck/head dip. 4 deep dip with beak near ground. 5 first ground-contact peck. 6 small head recoil. 7 second contact peck. 8 small recoil. 9 third contact peck. 10 raise neck halfway. 11 nearly upright. 12 fully upright matching frame 1 for seamless loop. Beak must reach ground in deep peck frames, neck flexes anatomically and body/wing shape stays same identity. Feet stay at the SAME local cell coordinate, subtle tail counterbalance. Clear distinct pecking poses. A compact 1.2 second loop at 10fps, inspired by sheep grazing dip-and-return timing. All twelve cells must align to a precise grid.
